evidence: Traupman 62: ē lectō surgere, to get out of bed

terms.gloss: rise up, get to one’s feet
evidence: Traupman 57: nōn omnīnō cōnsurgere possum, I can’t get up at all
terms.comment: Rising together or rising all the way up, as from a seat or the ground.

phrases.english: get up and walk: Dad, lifting the sleeping boy out of bed (Mt 9, 5, in jest)

sources: Lewis & Short: surgo · Dickinson: Latin Core Vocabulary
